sampling context together.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

L3 oral-exposure records for quaternary ammonium antimuscarinics trospium and glycopyrronium show pg/mL-level Cmax and low AUC after oral doses (trospium Cmax 1517–2717 pg/mL, AUC24 ~14,900–28,590 pg·h/mL; glycopyrronium Cmax 318 pg/mL after 2 mg), consistent with low oral systemic exposure.

L4 shows trospium has high aqueous solubility (>100 mg/mL), so the low oral exposure in this class is not solubility-limited; the barrier is consistent with permeability limitation from the permanent positive charge.

L5 gut-wall evidence does not overturn low: quaternary ammonium tropane antimuscarinics can be substrates of uptake transporters (OCTN2 for ipratropium/tiotropium; OCT1/OCT2 for trospium), but trospium oral absorption was not improved by ranitidine inhibition of OCT1/P-gp (C170), and tropane analogs can show high efflux ratios (C195). Ion-pair enhancement for propantheline (C193) is a formulation mechanism, not intrinsic high F.
